item.title: [IGNITE-8984] Ignite 2.5 - Vulnerabilities
item.description: Recently we have scanned Apache Ignite 2.5 source code and all the associated maven packages using Blackduck. The scan identified with many of the dependencies for Ignite 2.5. Many of these vulnerabilities are rated as High risk vulnerabilities. I've attached the vulnerability report to this ticket.

status.description: A resolution has been taken, and it is awaiting verification by reporter. From here issues are either reopened, or are closed.

dmagda navulirs, FYI:
Ignite-gce and its depencency Apache HttpComponents Client has warnings about medium risk vulnerabitilies:

  • CVE-2011-1498
  • CVE-2012-6153
  • CVE-2014-3577
  • CVE-2015-5262

But it seems nothing can be done with this warnings:

  • Google API client 1.22.0 depends on google-http-client-jackson2 (see also https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/com.google.api-client/google-api-client/1.22.0 )
  • Google-http-client-jackson2 depends on google-http-client (see
    https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/com.google.http-client/google-http-client-jackson2/1.22.0 )
  • And google-http-client depends on org.apache.httpcomponents httpclient v 4.0.1 (see https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/com.google.http-client/google-http-client/1.22.0 )

New version of Google HTTP client stil contains reference to 4.0.1 (
https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/com.google.http-client/google-http-client/1.23.0 )

So it is not possible to update Google API client version. Ignite itself declares httpclient.version as 4.5.1 - it is quite fresh version.

Same it true for guava 17.0 warning on CVE-2018-10237. Google API client specifies dependency in its own pom.
And newest client: https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/com.google.api-client/google-api-client/1.23.0 references to guava 17.0 jdk-5 version, which is not controlled by us.
We can’t override dependency version because it cause uncontrolled failures, even in runtime.
